taxonomy_mapping_dispositions.reason: Private chatbot interaction and public Discover publication were materially different access states, yet the share workflow reportedly left some users unsure that the resulting post would be public.

A separate share action and preview are evidenced, but unclear public audience/state leaves sufficient authority revalidation for recipients, persistence and downstream effect unproved. The new action engages the invariant without establishing all success conditions or automatic carry-over failure.

dimensions.assessment_basis: The preserved sources establish the bounded consequence described in the Incident summary: Meta's standalone AI app included a Discover feed through which users could publish chatbot conversations. Reporting found sensitive medical, legal, relationship, audio and identifying information publicly visible, while some users appeared not to understand that their shared conversations would be public. Meta maintained that publishing required an affirmative share action. Unreported downstream consequences were not inferred. Threshold applied: Meaningful bounded exposure, access or misuse of personal, credential or confidential information that is substantially containable.
